name: Descarboxylysergic acid
summary: Descarboxylysergic acid (DCLA), or 8-descarboxylysergic acid, also known as 9,10-didehydro-6-methylergoline or as 6-methyl-9-ergolene, is a drug of the ergoline and partial lysergamide families related to lysergic acid and lysergamides like lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD). It is the analogue of lysergic acid in which the carboxyl group at the C8 position of the molecule has been removed.

pharmacology.text: Subsequent research by David E. Nichols found that DCLA did not show LSD-like effects in animal drug discrimination tests. According to Nichols, the simplest ergoline with definite known psychoactive effects in humans is the lysergamide lysergic acid amide (LSA; ergine).
